newsitem.title: USA: Sprint to buy Paranet for $425 million.
newsitem.headline: Sprint to buy Paranet for $425 million.

text.p: Sprint Corp., aiming to broaden its network systems management business, said Monday it agreed to buy Paranet Inc. for $425 million in cash.

Called "Sprint Paranet," the new business unit will provide network and systems management services that will allow more companies to outsource all or part of the design, implementation and management of their distributed computing infrastructure, the company said.

"Many businesses are asking Sprint to help them simplify the design and management of their network systems," said William T. Esrey, chairman and chief executive officer of Sprint. "Sprint Paranet gives our customers much needed access to high-quality, proven services that help fully exploit the competitive advantage of properly-utilized network assets."

Sprint said nearly 50 percent of all businesses already outsource some or all of their network and system management needs. The U.S. market for network management services currently represents a $27 billion business segment and is expected to grow to a $43 billion market by the year 2000, it said.

"This is not just a technology issue, but an integration of hardware, software, networks and people, which produces the highly productive environments that give companies a competitive edge," said Michael H. Holthouse, president and founder of Houston-based Paranet.
Holthouse has been appointed president of Sprint Paranet.

As part of Sprint, the Sprint Paranet unit will design and deliver networks using networking and system components from throughout the industry. This will allow Sprint Paranet to preserve the customers' investments in existing equipment, while migrating them to new and more effective technology.
With 1,100 employees, Paranet has more than 900 technical analysts in 25 U.S. cities. It serves more than 250 major customers.
Paranet recorded 1996 revenues of $66 million, and revenues are expected to be approximately double in 1997.
Sprint has $14 billion in annual revenues and serves more than 16 million business and residential customers.
The acquisition is expected to be completed by the end of 1997.
